Shelokmengi (S57)

Survey-table region: Sarhal.

In brief: Let priests govern the weather, let granaries sustain the army, and let a young king turn a valley of nobles into an administrative state.

Story: High | Mission-tree length: Medium (25 directly defined missions) | Mission-tree update: Dedicated tree in the current local build | Distinctiveness: High | Tedium: Medium | Early pressure: Medium-high | Expansion: Upper-medium. Checked against the base mod and localisation supporting EU4 v1.37.5.0; the older count of 27 is not used.

Identity and history

Shelokmengi is a valley kingdom among the Mengi states of eastern Sarhal. Its culture is Yetferi and its faith is the Court of the Sky. Fertile river valleys, rather than mineral wealth or defensible mountain passes, are its foundation: their grain has long fed nearby cities, making farmland, temples, and river transport central to politics.【Local history script】【Local narrative text】

In 1444, a council of nobles governs as regent; the young heir Ayufar has not yet ruled in his own right. The history file establishes the regency and heir in 1438. The mission narrative tells of Queen Almaz's struggle with the regent nobles and of Ayufar II's later attempt to curb their military power, recruit talent, and build an administrative system. His accession and reforms are campaign developments, not completed facts about 1444.【Local history script】【Local localisation】

The offline Wiki stub calls the ruler Ayufar II, matching the local history and mission localisation, and says he reformed the state into an administrative kingdom that later consolidated the region and proclaimed the Second Merakh Mengi. The stub does not provide a detailed chronology for these reforms.【Wiki】【Local history script】【Local localisation】

National story and campaign arc

This campaign is not about a king who begins with absolute power. It is about recovering initiative from the institutions left by a noble regency. The nobles retain military power and local influence; Ayufar instead builds another source of fiscal and productive power by relying on priests, mages, scholars, and experts from abroad.【Local narrative text】

Grain temples and mills connect religion to industry, while rain-priests regulate the weather for agriculture. An early, unstable design also risks grain-dust fires; later, windmills are placed beside temples so priests can fight fires more easily. The “weather kingdom” therefore has concrete labour, construction, and safety concerns, not merely a magical button to press in battle.【Local narrative text】

In the middle and later campaign, nobles are permanently invited to reside at court, while stewards or royal appointees manage their lands. Missions also call for more Crown Land, the removal of noble military privileges, and administrative reform. Regional unification may ultimately lead to Merakh Mengi, but completing 25 missions does not automatically create an empire spanning the whole region.【Local script】【Local narrative text】

Core mechanics

First is the Court of the Sky's weather actions. Missions, clergy, and mage relations unlock abilities. The fair-weather action costs 100 religious power and has a three-year cooldown. The sudden-flood action costs 50 and requires a besieged fort in a province still controlled by your country. They serve management and defence respectively; not every weather spell is an always-available offensive tool.【Local script】

Second is granary reform. As reforms advance, the script replaces national modifiers in stages, increasing manpower recovery and land force limit, reducing recruitment costs, and eventually unlocking supply depots. Grain provinces, production buildings, temples, and the army form a loop: expansion acquires farmland, and farms plus reform sustain a larger military. This is more than a tax-stacking economy.【Local script】

Third is the redistribution of power between king and estates. Crown Land, noble military privileges, and the loyalty of clergy and mages are real prerequisites; conquest alone cannot substitute for domestic preparation. Fourth is the Harimari policy choice. The expulsion/low-tolerance route removes minorities and changes culture in exchange for money. The high-tolerance and racial-focus route instead adds minorities, improves diplomacy, and grants a merchant modifier. Expulsion is not an unavoidable ending for every player.【Local script】

Phased play and formation

Early on, protect the succession after the regency and the treasury, invest in grain infrastructure, and manage pressure from neighbouring states. Treat relations with the clergy and mages as development resources, rather than focusing only on the nobles' immediate military convenience. In the midgame, use rain-priests and granaries to support war, gradually reclaim Crown Land, reform the administration, and develop river ports and networks of foreign experts.

The late-game formation of Merakh Mengi (L65) requires the Court of the Sky faith and an eligible Mengi culture, at least 75 provinces in specified areas, control of six of eight key cities, peace, and the required autonomy conditions. The decision changes the Tag, raises the country's rank, and changes its ideas. The decision checked here contains no explicit mission-swap instruction; it therefore does not establish that unfinished S57-specific missions remain available after formation, nor does it verify a dedicated successor tree.【Local decision】

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 72/100 | Autocracy 78/100 | Magic–Artifice 90/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 83/100) | Pluralism 45/100. The autocracy profile changes by phase: noble regency (48) → Ayufar's administrative kingship (78).

The v2.1 values classification is Neutral (56/100), with a branch-dependent trajectory: the Harimari tolerant-trade route (Neutral 65/100) → the Harimari expulsion route (Neutral 40/100).

The explanatory v2.1 profile is Expansion 72 | Autocracy 78 | Magic direction 90 (theme intensity 83) | Pluralism 45. Early aristocratic decentralisation and later royal administrative centralisation have separate phase profiles; weakening nobles does not automatically give ordinary people freedom. Rain-priests, weather-working and religious agriculture support the magical direction, not merely the presence of a character called a mage.

The v2.1 values score is Neutral (56), with a branch-dependent trajectory: dignity 48, public good 82, personhood 45, and restraint 52. The Harimari tolerant-trade route is assessed at Neutral (65), while the expulsion route is Neutral (40). Neither removes the documented background of enslaved harvest labour. Agricultural improvements, public shipping, and recruitment of outside experts are positive evidence; the low-tolerance branch explicitly calls for exclusion of a minority population. The score is not reduced merely for monarchy, centralisation, war, or regional unification, and minority removal is not inflated into an unverified claim of massacre.

This country suits players who enjoy grain economics, estate politics, religious magic, and a medium-length story of political development. Avoid it if you want uninterrupted conquest, do not want to manage estates and reforms, or expect a verified, very long post-formation tree.

Community experience and evidence limits

Official Dev Diary 80 presents a valley kingdom where a young king, nobles, and priests compete, and discusses Mengi unification. A 2025-09-06 campaign report praised the weather actions and character story, but its author explicitly reloaded several times to keep the ruler alive, so it is not a measure of ordinary difficulty. A 2026-08-10 discussion concerned a missing reform option without the Domination DLC; it is a reminder to check which features are available in one's own installation, not proof that every step requires that DLC.【Official dev diary】【Community view】

The current English country name is Shelokmengi, not the older split spelling used in some searches. A complete Wiki history for its successor, post-formation mission reachability, and historical-map materials remain gaps. See the evidence record for the precise sources.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Shelokmengi (S57) — Shelokmengi Ideas

Set ID: S57_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = S57 #Shelokmengi
    }

Shelokmengi Traditions

  • National tax modifier: +10% (global_tax_modifier; raw value 0.10).

  • Infantry Cost: -10% (infantry_cost; raw value -0.10).

1. Breadbasket Of The Mengi

Shelokmengi, the valley kingdom, controlled some of the most fertile and productive farmlands in East Sarhal. Though it lacked great mineral wealth or defensible positions, the land was rich in its own right, and crops sprang from the soil here as if they longed to be picked by human hands. The fertile potential of the valley was noticed ages ago, and it has produced vast harvests of wheat, barley and sorghum for millennia, sustaining the great cities of Yeteferen.

  • Production efficiency: +10% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.10).

2. The Yet Bend

The great Yet river coils as a serpent, ebbing and flowing, and near the lands of Shelokmengi it makes a great bend across the land. Highly navigable, the river has acted as a natural highway for the Yeteferen peoples since time immemorial. Shelokmengi’s many villages are all located near or on the great Yet bend, allowing easy access to merchant vessels, who will happily buy the vast harvests of Shelokmengi and sell them to the cities upon the length of the Yet.

  • Domestic trade power: +10% (global_own_trade_power; raw value 0.10).

3. Yemane The Secretary

The harvest requires much work. One must keep track of the laborers, the seeds to be planted, the amount of crops sold, the time of the year, and more. Every farmer of Shelokmengi became adept at skills that were also useful in administration, and so the kings of Shelokmengi found no shortage of competent administrators among the population.

This great administrative skill was best embodied in Yemane ‘The Secretary’. Born a farmer, Yemane originally owned only a small piece of land. His great administrative skills and wit allowed him to increase the yields of his farm manyfold, and he began to increase the yields of other farms in the local villages. Eventually, he would be noticed by Ayufar II during one of his yearly harvest processions, was recognized for this skill, and hired as the king’s personal secretary.

Yemane would be a crucial advisor to Ayufar II for most of his reign, being responsible for many administrative reforms in the kingdom. His most legendary feat was the mobilization of 10,000 men in a single month, although according to Yemane, it was no more than another task akin to organizing the harvest.

  • Administrative advisor cost: -25% (adm_advisor_cost; raw value -0.25).

4. The Battle Of Berfan

In 1452 the trolls of Yezel Mora broke their usual border raids by doing something not seen since the rule of Zenidir the Shadowslayer - an invasion of Madriamilak. Following the rise of Adurmag the Dreadful, an army of trolls invaded Shelokmengi with the goal of burning the whole of the Yet river valley and sacking the great city of Yetmetsira by the ocean. When news of the host came, the Mezhi of Shelokmengi called to arms every able bodied man to defend the holy land, of which only 9,760 warriors and 108 magi gathered in time when news of the trolls crossing the border arrived.

At a small walled lumber town that bridged a tributary of the Yet did the army of Shelokmengi clash with Adurmag’s horde. Here with spear and shield the Shelokmengi held for 14 days, slaying nearmost 2,000 trolls until they finally breached the walls. At this point the Mengi withdrew over the bridge and out of the town. A feigned rout, as the Mengi held the trolls in the town whilst the deviousness of their trap was revealed. The magi had been channeling the very air and sky itself to create a beam of light so intense that it could catch buildings aflame. Sawdust soaked in seed oil caught alight in a great conflagration that instantly incinerated half the horde as it had clamored into the village, including Adurmag himself. That day, the Shadow Trolls feared not their masters, but the Shelokmengi.

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

5. A Blessing In Disguise

The death of Afwerki III at the gates of Enikmesiki in 1438 was a disaster for Shelokmengi. His young son was left in the hands of a squabbling regency council, bent on turning the young king Ayufar II into a puppet.

When Ayufar II came of age to rule, however, he was not what the lesser-kings expected him to be. One of the most capable and ruthless administrators of his day, he was keen to crack down on those that had led his father to ruin, including the former members of the regency council. He stamped out the corrupt nobles, confiscating the lands of those that dared defy him and placing loyalists into their positions.

By the time Ayufar reached the age of 38, he had completely destroyed any internal resistance in his kingdom. Thus he finally declared war on Enikmesiki, seeking revenge for his fathers murder and hunting those nobles who had fled his vengeance. He at last took the city where his father had been killed in 1474, his revenge complete.

Years later, when asked what his thoughts of the Enikmesiki "incident" was, he quipped, "Enikmesiki may have been a catastrophe, but it was also a blessing in disguise."

  • Nobility loyalty equilibrium: +5% (nobles_loyalty_modifier; raw value 0.05).

  • Yearly corruption: -0.05 (yearly_corruption; raw value -0.05).

6. The Harvest Procession

Every Yeteferen kingdom may have a harvest festival, but Shelokmengi has a harvest procession. When the harvest season begins, the king of Shelokmengi leaves his palace and travels the land in a great procession. These processions acted as moving harvest festivals, with massive amounts of food given away for free. It was very common for the harvest processions of Shelokmengi to move into other kingdoms, as the kings of Shelokmengi sought to flaunt their wealth in the face of their rivals. These harvest processions showed all the richness of Shelokmengi, and the benefits of its rule. Most importantly, it made the lower classes happy and loyal to the kings of Shelokmengi.

  • National unrest: -2 (global_unrest; raw value -2).

7. Direct Rule From The Palace

The successors of Ayufar II would continue his work of centralizing and pacifying the realm and the lesser-kings. By the late 16th century, the lesser-kings of Shelokmengi had been weakened to the point where they merely served as hereditary administrators, with almost all real power in the kingdom resting in the hands of the king and his close circle of advisors in the great palace in Berfan.

  • global_autonomy：-0.05% (global_autonomy; raw value -0.05).

Shelokmengi Ambitions

  • global_manpower_modifier：+20% (global_manpower_modifier; raw value 0.20).

Melakmengi (L65) — Melakmengi Ideas

Set ID: L65_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = L65 #Melakmengi
    }

Melakmengi Traditions

  • Construction cost: -10% (build_cost; raw value -0.1).

  • Army morale: +10% (land_morale; raw value 0.1).

1. Zenidir's Legacy

The Legacy of Zenidir the Shadowslayer is a great one. Over the course of over 500 years, Zenidir’s rule saw the spread of the Yeteferen language across Madriamilak, which eventually evolved into the modern Mengi language. Their actions sought to uplift the nomadic tribes of what would become Madriamilak, directing the construction of over a hundred cities and settlements over his reign. Uplifting thousands to a better, more civilized life, Zenidir helped codify the laws of the land and bring peace to a realm savaged by the dark forces of Yezel Mora. With Melakmengi reborn, we will do the same as they did, and seek to better the lives of all of Amilak’s subjects.

  • Years of separatism: -5 (years_of_nationalism; raw value -5).

2. The Semayebaka Society

The importance of magic users cannot be understated. Magic among the Mengi themselves is primarily divided into two districts of authority, the Tanikweya and the Semayebaka. The forces associated with the wind, skies, and waters are entrusted to the Semayebaka, the Cloud-mages and Rain-priests. In modern Melakmengi, they are quite influential as they are the primary deliverers of rites, and rituals that see crops irrigated and the land kept clean. Through the institution of the Semayebaka Society, a recently-founded conclave of high ranking Semayebaka that works closely with the state, the various magical clergy of Melakmengi can be directed to serve the interests of the state more effectively.

  • English translation: [Country.GetMageName]: +10% (mages_loyalty_modifier; raw value 0.1).

3. An End To The Trollish Menace

For thousands of years we have fought an unending war against the armies of Yrilak. Periodically they march out from the Yezel Mora and desolate our lands. Their devilish features, unmatched stature, incredible regeneration abilities and harsh homeland make the trolls an undefeatable enemy. With time we developed techniques to destroy the troll, yet we were still left at a fundamental disadvantage. For as long as a single troll still stands, Madriamilak is not safe.

However in the 16th century, the cannon appeared in our ports, brought in by Raheni and Cannorian merchants. We readily adopted the weaponry and made it our own, producing our own variants and designs, many of which found use against the trolls of the Yezel Mora. Artillery finally gave us the advantage against our hated enemies, and as such it will always carry a central role in Mengi tactics and strategy.

  • Artillery combat ability: +15% (artillery_power; raw value 0.15).

4. God Of The Skies

"Amilak has sent a portent to me this morn from the heavens, of a flock of five birds - the Hill Sparrow, the Cliff Falcon, the Golden Eagle, the River Thrush, and the Ofehibi Crane. Each in unison flew across the sky until they landed upon a dead tree, where other birds - the Savannah Swallow of the northern lands, the Blue Coua of the Dakinshi and a hundred more of lands further beyond who perched upon the lower branches. All bowed in reverence to the great eagle that arrived last, a great beast who sat upon the highest perch with pure white wings. The message was clear. Amilak had begun his war to unite the God-Kin, and we must do the same upon this world."

  • High Priest Yenetoti, 1737, Declaration of Unity

  • Missionaries: +1 (missionaries; raw value 1).

  • Manpower from true faith provinces: +15% (manpower_in_true_faith_provinces; raw value 0.15).

5. Order Of Rains

The Order of Rains is a conclave and section of the Semayebaka Society that is invested with the holy duties of summoning rain and moderating dangerous storms. Local Mezhi and freeholders work closely with representatives from the Order to ensure farm fields regularly receive rain, with timetables scheduled months in advance. In some regions this is further streamlined as peace and unity over Madriamilak allows wider access to an education system that produces masses of rain priests. The inevitable result is increasingly large crop yields, allowing even the poorest Mengi to be fed regularly by a steady subsidy of grain procured by the state.

  • Development cost: -15% (development_cost; raw value -0.15).

6. A New Administration For A New Empire

The first Melakmengi Empire was an absolute monarchy, the Mezhi`Mezhi Zenidir Zentirizar wielding absolute authority. Yet in practice it governed like a confederation, governors being assigned to the 10 regions of the empire, who ruled like kings in Zenidir’s stead. Later Mengi historians and statesmen came to criticize this style of rule as uniquely unstable, only held together by the force of will of a dragon.

When the second Melakmengi Empire formed, its rulers chose to not emulate Zenidir’s style of rule, and instead invited scholars and administrators from Rahen and Yanshen, seeking to build an efficient bureaucratic government and a centralized empire. With this new army of administrators, successive Mezhi`Mezhi chipped away at and ultimately destroyed the feudal power structures that stubbornly refused to die, in an era that made the lesser-lords increasingly irrelevant.

  • Governing Capacity Modifier: +15% (governing_capacity_modifier; raw value 0.15).

7. The Nagide Monopoly

For millennia foreign merchants have come to Madriamilak, bringing with them new ideas and wealth. However, these foreigners grew in power and influence along the coastline, a parasitic relationship that eventually destroyed the coastal Ofehibi kingdoms in the 15th century. In the 16th and 17th centuries, Cannorian traders started to appear along the eastern coast, bringing new technologies, but also destabilizing ideas that went against Amilak’s truth.

The 2nd Melakmengi Empire took a very different approach to the kingdoms that preceded it. In 1758, the Mezhi’Mezhi decreed the creation of what became known as "The Nagide Monopoly", a system of monopolies and free trade zones in Dakmender and Yetmesira into which foreigners could enter to do business, while being prohibited from venturing deeper into Madriamilak, by force if necessary. Domestic merchant companies needed a license from the state to trade with foreign merchants, with the state taking a comfortable percentage of the profits.

  • Trade efficiency: +10% (trade_efficiency; raw value 0.10).

Melakmengi Ambitions

  • True faith tolerance: +2 (tolerance_own; raw value 2).
